newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade below 3,000 points.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade below 3,000 points.

text.p: German equities ended bourse trade lower on Friday in sympathy with Wall Street's overnight tumble, but dealers said this was not the large-scale correction many have been waiting for.
The DAX-30 index ended at 2,998.24 points, down 35.22 points or 1.16 percent, after a wave programme-selling dragged the Dow Jones index to a sharply lower close overnight.
March DAX futures were down 47.4 points at 3,000.5, just barely above the psychological 3,000-point level.
Wall Street had finished lower on a wave of "programme" selling, where computers have been programmed to initiate sell orders once a certain set of conditions have been fulfilled.
"This is not a catastrophe," said one dealer. "It's being seen by some as an opportunity to buy," she noted.

Another dealer confirmed that even despite the fact that it was a Friday, where market players are traditionally not keen to take significant new positions in the market, there was little chance of the losses being extended -- at least until Wall Street's open later today.
"Fundamentally, there is nothing wrong with the market and the currency situation is still positive," he said.
The dollar traded at 1.6280 marks, still firm if slightly down on earlier levels. German bund futures however were lower, in tune with a drop in U.S. Treasuries.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG bucked the trend to end bourse up 3.50 marks at 769.50 after the U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers rated it its best pick among European auto stocks for 1997.

Shares in industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG slipped 1.95 marks to end at 114.10, in line with the market fall, despite a newspaper report that it saw sales rising to around 130 billion marks by the year 2000 from a current 106 billion.
Chief financial officer Manfred Gentz also said in an interview with the Handeslblatt newspaper he did not expect the group to seek to raise any capital this year.
